question: On actual already-consumed public action/consequence records, does bounded feedback on confidently wrong predictions improve an existing native forecast more than frozen memory and equally budgeted random feedback? Can normal all-feedback learning outperform selective correction?

design.native: Unchanged PublicCausalCells128 learned bytes/164 checkpoint bytes, same16 addresses and Beta(1,1) readout. No native runtime modification.
design.initial_knowledge: All previously frozen24 public events/world,96 distinct events total; cloned immutable initial checkpoint, never rewritten.
design.feedback_stream: The remaining7 already-consumed events/world,28 total, ordered round-robin index24..30 then world0..3. Predict both outputs BEFORE revealing current feedback to update. Future row values never used by learners/gates.
design.confidence: Fixed inclusive posterior>=3/4 predicting1 or<=1/4 predicting0; confidently wrong means observed current outcome is the opposite. Observational stochastic misses do NOT prove incorrect world law.
design.all_feedback: Assimilate each newly witnessed event until shared maximum event cap; two outcome updates/event.
design.error_only: After predictions and current feedback, if ANY target was confidently wrong and cap remains, assimilate that entire new event once.
design.random_matched: Update at EXACT SAME times and in same world as error_only, exactlyone event/trigger. Choose an as-yet-unlearned newly witnessed event from that world's prefix by minimumSHA256(canon([seed,cap,world,current_index,candidate_index])). No future rows, no repeat, no using previously trained24 as fresh evidence. These compare subset assignment conditional on error_only's gate; not independent deployed policies.
design.strong_control: Independently fitted exact Beta probabilities using each arm's actual event ledger. Both outputs must match native at every decision. all_feedback uses the same maximum cap and public information but may consume more observations than error_only; disclose realized costs and do not claim equal realized cost there.
design.scores: Brier mean over SAME56 output predictions, wrong-confident counts, exact rational differences vs frozen, paired trace hashes. Score before feedback, never rescore repaired model on the label used to update it.
design.retention: Every update keeps other worlds'24 posterior readouts unchanged; all original192 counter increments remain componentwise, verify independently against event-ledger counts, final cold snapshot byte identity and forecasts.
design.negative_controls: Future event, duplicate event and malformed row rejected before partial update; same initial frozen checkpoint remains unchanged.

thresholds.primary: At max28 cap error_only pooled Brier at least0.005 lower than frozen AND at least0.005 lower than mean matched-random Brier, otherwise exploratory NO_GO. Strong equally informed exact-Beta comparison must be tie; cannot establish superiority.
thresholds.secondary: Report all-feedback/frozen and descending-cap curves without choosing new settings.
thresholds.reason: All labels were consumed historically. Retrospective mechanism falsification only; no independent new-world confirmation.

qualification: Focused negatives/chronology/reference/cold mechanics first; mandatory full root and NKR05 regression plus independent G29 on final candidate BOTH OS; preserve all old results and original checkpoint. Existing draft1172 only.
